newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Lithuania says Gazprom may cut supplies.
newsitem.headline: Lithuania says Gazprom may cut supplies.

text.p: Lithuania's state-owned gas company Lithuania Gas on Wednesday said Russian gas giant Gazprom has threatened to halve its supplies in February if progress was not made on a $41 million debt.

"Gazprom sent a telegram on Monday to Prime Minister Vagnorius saying it would cut our gas supply by 50 percent on February 1 if measures were not taken to begin paying our $41 million debt," a Lithuania Gas spokesman told Reuters.
He said Gazprom was due to supply Lithuania with 70 million cubic meters of gas in February.
He added that an intermediary company Stella Vitae was due to send Lithuania 234 million cubic meters of gas in February.
Lithuania Gas owes Gazprom $28.5 million directly and $12.5 million to Stella Vitae, which it in turn owes to Gazprom.
This cycle of debt is common in Lithuania's inefficient and debt-ridden energy sector. Consumers often fail to pay producers who in turn are unable to pay suppliers.
The current government has promised to privatise big chunks of the sector in an effort to make it more efficient and more responsive to market conditions.
